title: Wexler Ave Memorial Incident
premise: A spontaneous memorial for a recent fatal shooting in a Chicago neighborhood turns violent when a lone officer draws his sidearm, prompting a crowd of hundreds to surge forward before backup arrives.

side_A.role: a researcher at a human-rights NGO
side_A.goal: documenting possible excessive force by police against protesters

side_B.goal: preparing criminal charges against protesters for rioting and property damage

documents:
=== DOCUMENT 1: Incident Log and Radio Transcripts - Chicago Police Department ===

**INCIDENT REPORT NO:** 23-1012-449
**LOCATION:** Intersection of Wexler Ave and 4th Street, Southside District
**DATE:** October 12, 2023
**OFFICER ON DUTY:** Marcus Thorne, Badge #4921
**STATUS:** Closed

**1. INITIAL RESPONSE AND ARRIVAL**
At 19:12, Officer Marcus Thorne arrived at the scene in Patrol Unit 74. The unit arrived alone; no additional officers were present at the scene at the time of arrival. The area contained a gathering of approximately 50 individuals situated near the pedestrian crosswalk.

**2. RADIO LOG EXTRACT**
*   **19:15:02** [Thorne to Dispatch]: "Unit 74 requesting backup to Wexler and 4th. Crowd is becoming unmanageable. Requesting immediate support."
*   **19:15:05** [Dispatch to Thorne]: "Copy, Unit 74. Backup en route. Stay safe."
*   **19:31:10** [Dispatch to Thorne]: "Units 22 and 30 are on scene. Stand by for handoff."

*Note: Backup units arrived at 19:31, which is seven minutes after the initial request for assistance.*

**3. EVIDENCE LOG**
*   **Item 101:** Bystander video file, "Wexler_Memorial_1845.mp4," submitted by anonymous citizen.
*   **Item 102:** Security camera footage from 24-hour laundromat at 1415 Wexler Ave.
*   **Item 103:** Corrupted body camera file, Unit 74. File integrity check failed. Footage is unplayable from timestamp 19:22:00 to 19:25:00.
*   **Item 104:** Digital clock overlay from Laundromat camera showing time 19:24:14.

**4. PROPERTY DAMAGE**
A 2017 Ford F-150 pickup truck, driven by citizen J. Miller, was struck by a projectile. The front bumper sustained denting. The projectile was recovered and identified as a standard 2-inch gravel stone.

**5. PERSONNEL INJURIES**
Three individuals in the crowd were transported to the local emergency room. Medical personnel diagnosed them with mild concussion injuries. The injuries resulted from being struck by falling debris from a nearby storefront awning.

=== DOCUMENT 2: Witness Statement of Dr. Elena Rostova ===

**STATEMENT OF DR. ELENA ROSTOVA**
**Date of Statement:** October 14, 2023
**Role:** Researcher/NGO Representative

I was present at the memorial gathering on Wexler Avenue and 4th Street. It was a somber, peaceful event. I have a ten-year history of mediating community disputes, and in all that time, I have never recorded an instance of violence from the groups I work with. We were simply standing there, honoring the deceased.

At 18:45, I was recorded on a bystander’s phone speaking into a megaphone. I was directing the crowd to remain in the pedestrian crosswalk, which is where we belonged. We were respectful.

When Officer Thorne arrived at 19:12, he did not attempt to talk to us. He stood there, looking aggressive. I watched him closely. He was visibly intoxicated. He was stumbling before the confrontation even began. His movements were erratic, and he lacked the steady posture of a professional officer. This compromised his ability to de-escalate the situation safely. It was clear to anyone watching that he was impaired.

The crowd surged forward only because Officer Thorne drew his sidearm and pointed it at the gathering. He created an immediate threat perception. We did not move out of malice; we moved because he made us feel unsafe.

Regarding the physical contact, I can state clearly that police officers made the first physical contact. After the surge began, Thorne and the arriving backup shoved the front row of the crowd back. This action escalated the violence. I was located 50 meters away from the officer when the crowd began to surge, so I had a clear view of the entire sequence. The officers were the aggressors in that moment, pushing people who were merely trying to be heard.

I also want to note that at 19:20, I explicitly told the crowd, "Do not advance toward the officer." This was to keep the peace, not to incite. The audio analysis of my megaphone recording confirms this. The crowd was not trying to harm him. We were trying to survive his aggression.

=== DOCUMENT 3: Witness Statement of Officer Marcus Thorne ===

**STATEMENT OF OFFICER MARCUS THORNE**
**Date of Statement:** October 15, 2023
**Role:** Chicago Police Department, Badge #4921

I have served 12 years with the Chicago Police Department. I have dealt with hundreds of crowds, and I know how to handle them. I arrived at the scene at 19:12 to manage a situation that was already volatile.

I request backup at 19:15 because the crowd was becoming unmanageable. This is standard procedure for a growing crowd. It is not a sign of impairment, as some have claimed. I was alert and professional. I was performing my duty to ensure public safety.

The crowd surged forward because an unidentified individual in the back of the line began throwing objects. This forced a defensive reaction from the officers. I did not draw my weapon to threaten anyone; I drew it because I was being attacked. The first physical contact was made by the crowd. A protester grabbed my baton, prompting the officers to clear the area to prevent further injury.

I was not intoxicated. I was focused on the threat. The crowd was attempting to breach the police line and physically tackle the officer. I saw the aggressive forward momentum and heard the shouts. They were not peaceful. They were a violent mob trying to overpower me.

The debris that fell from the awning was a result of the chaos created by the crowd’s aggression. I did not shove anyone. I maintained my position until backup arrived. The narrative that I was stumbling is false. I was doing my job under fire.

=== DOCUMENT 4: Witness Statement of Mr. Silas Vane ===

**STATEMENT OF MR. SILAS VANE**
**Date of Statement:** October 16, 2023
**Role:** Memorial Organizer

I organized the memorial for the victim of the recent fatal shooting. We did not file a prior permit with the City of Chicago Parks and Recreation Department because we believed a spontaneous gathering at an intersection did not require one. We were wrong, but our intent was peaceful.

I was present at the scene. I was not visible in any of the captured video footage until 19:26. Before that, I was moving through the crowd to check on people.

The crowd was attempting to surround the officer to demand an apology for the recent fatal shooting, not to physically assault him. We wanted answers. We wanted justice. When Officer Thorne arrived, he was not helpful. He was not listening.

I disagree with the idea that we were trying to tackle him. We were trying to talk to him. But when he reacted with force, it changed everything. The crowd’s movement was a reaction to his hostility. We were not a mob; we were mourners.

I saw Officer Thorne act erratically. I believe he was not in the right state of mind. But regardless of his condition, the police response was disproportionate. We were just standing there, trying to be heard.

=== DOCUMENT 5: Witness Statement of Citizen J. Miller ===

**STATEMENT OF CITIZEN J. MILLER**
**Date of Statement:** October 16, 2023
**Role:** Bystander/Driver

I was driving my 2017 Ford F-150 past the intersection when the trouble started. I saw the crowd from my vehicle. They were not just standing there. They were pushing. They were shouting.

The crowd was attempting to breach the police line and physically tackle the officer. I saw the aggressive forward momentum. I saw people in the front row reaching out. It looked like they were going to grab him.

I heard the shouts. They were angry. They were not peaceful. I pulled over because I was afraid for the officer’s safety. Then, a stone hit my truck. It was a standard 2-inch gravel stone. It dented my front bumper. I was lucky it didn’t hit anyone else.

I did not see Officer Thorne stumble or look drunk. He looked like a cop doing his job. He was holding his ground. The crowd was the problem. They were trying to overwhelm him. I think the officer had no choice but to defend himself.

=== DOCUMENT 6: Witness Statement of Sergeant Alan Pierce ===

**STATEMENT OF SERGEANT ALAN PIERCE**
**Date of Statement:** October 17, 2023
**Role:** Police Supervisor, Chicago Police Department

I reviewed the incident on Wexler Avenue. Officer Thorne had served 12 years with the department before this incident. He is a veteran officer.

Officer Thorne was alert and professional; his request for backup was a standard procedure for a growing crowd, not a sign of impairment. I know Officer Thorne well. He does not drink on duty. The claim that he was stumbling is baseless.

The crowd was unmanageable. When an unidentified individual began throwing objects, the officer had to react. The first physical contact was made by the crowd when a protester grabbed the officer’s baton. The officers cleared the area to prevent further violence.

The backup units arrived at 19:31, seven minutes after the request. This delay is a concern, but it does not change the fact that the officer was acting within his rights. The crowd’s intent was to assault the officer. They were not there to apologize or to talk. They were there to cause chaos.

=== DOCUMENT 7: Medical Report - Cook County Hospital ===

**PATIENT REPORT**
**Date of Admission:** October 12, 2023
**Location:** Emergency Room, Cook County Hospital

**Patient 1:**
*   **Diagnosis:** Mild concussion.
*   **Mechanism of Injury:** Struck by falling debris from nearby storefront awning.
*   **Status:** Discharged after observation.

**Patient 2:**
*   **Diagnosis:** Mild concussion.
*   **Mechanism of Injury:** Struck by falling debris from nearby storefront awning.
*   **Status:** Discharged after observation.

**Patient 3:**
*   **Diagnosis:** Mild concussion.
*   **Mechanism of Injury:** Struck by falling debris from nearby storefront awning.
*   **Status:** Discharged after observation.

**Note:** All three patients reported being in the crowd at the intersection of Wexler Avenue and 4th Street at approximately 19:24.

=== DOCUMENT 8: Digital Forensics and Audio Analysis Report ===

**REPORT NO:** 23-1012-450
**DATE:** October 18, 2023
**ANALYST:** Department of Digital Forensics

**1. AUDIO ANALYSIS**
A recording of a megaphone used by Dr. Elena Rostova was analyzed.
*   **Timestamp 19:20:** The recording indicates Dr. Rostova explicitly stated, "Do not advance toward the officer."
*   **Context:** The statement was directed at the crowd.

**2. VIDEO TIMELINE**
*   **18:45:** Bystander phone video shows Dr. Rostova speaking into a megaphone.
*   **19:12:** Officer Thorne arrives at the scene.
*   **19:12 - 19:22:** Bystander footage from a window of 1420 Wexler Ave shows the crowd remaining stationary.
*   **19:22:00 - 19:25:00:** Officer Thorne’s body camera footage is corrupted and unplayable.
*   **19:24:00:** Distance between the officer’s initial position and the nearest member of the crowd was measured at 15 meters.
*   **19:24:14:** A digital clock in the window of the laundromat shows the time as 19:24:14.
*   **19:24:15:** Security camera from the adjacent 24-hour laundromat captures the crowd beginning to move forward.
*   **19:26:** Mr. Silas Vane first becomes visible in the captured video footage.

**3. ALCOHOL TEST**
*   **Time:** 22:30
*   **Subject:** Officer Marcus Thorne
*   **Result:** Blood alcohol concentration of 0.08%.
*   **Method:** Post-incident breath test.

**4. PERMIT STATUS**
*   **Record Check:** City of Chicago Parks and Recreation Department records show no prior permit filed for the memorial gathering at the intersection of Wexler Avenue and 4th Street.
